newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Bank of Melbourne says outlook strong.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Bank of Melbourne says outlook strong.

text.p: Regional bank, Bank of Melbourne Ltd said on Wednesday its outlook was strong and it expects continued success in all areas of its operations in the state of Victoria and interstate markets.
"The bank expects to grow its share of the Victorian personal banking market building on the success of the second half of the 1996 financial year," the bank said in a statement.
Bank of Melbourne earlier reported that its net profit before preference share dividends rose to A$91.21 million in the year to June 30, 1996 from A$78.92 million in the previous year.

The bank's chief executive, David Airey, said in a statement the profit increase had been posted against a background of continued intense competition in the established market of owner occupied and residential investment lending.
"Given this the 11 percent growth in the residential property lending portfolio to A$6.6 billion was pleasing and reflected a particularly successful second half for the bank," Airey said.
Bank of Melbourne said its competition remained strong and had intensified in the past few months.
It said interest rate reductions together with the widespread use of no application fee campaigns had positioned the banks to compete more agressively with the mortgage origination market.

"In response to contraction in margins the bank will continue to expand its cost efficient electronic banking facilities introducing new Automatic Teller Machines (ATMs) and extending the range of automated telephone banking facilities," the bank said.
Bank of Melbourne said its commercial banking activity was expected to remain steady as it built its presence in the Victorian market.
The bank said its acquisition of the Challenge Bank Victorian business was expected to be completed towards the end of calendar 1996.

Bank of Melbourne announced in May it would acquire the Victorian operations of Challenge bank Ltd and had agreed to pay the net asset value at completion plus a premium of A$69 million during the 1996/97 year.
"After allowing for the amortisation of goodwill the acquisition is expected to be positive for return on equity and earnings per share," the bank said.
